top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature invention: a magic-wavelength lattice cancels the trap light shift so many neutral atoms are interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, combining ensemble statistics with single-ion cleanliness. It has been reproduced and intercompared at the 10^-18 level by independent national laboratories and has already delivered physics (millimetre-scale redshift, constants and dark-matter bounds, many-body clocks). The Katori/Ye split by contribution type is clean. A stand-alone prize is sharper than P002, whose Hosono part is a separate, unrelated achievement with no common thread; P002 is still preferred to no award because B040 is secure within it.
recusal_note: No direct tie to Katori or Ye apparent from profile; she is a long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier and works in adjacent atomic, molecular and optical physics, which is a mild connection at most.
